decisions.reason: A rye country bread fits the firm's core assortment, cost little to add, and has its own page, so there is no pressing reason to withdraw it.
The premium raisin stollen is a publicly presented flagship that again won a gold medal from the Deutsches Brotinstitut, so dropping it is very unlikely.
A seeded rye mixed bread is a low-risk extension of the established bread range with no sign of trouble, so it will likely stay.
A dark malt rye bread is a niche variant with little invested or committed in public, so it carries some pruning risk but most likely remains.
The marzipan stollen complements the seasonal flagship stollen line and is a typical recurring Christmas item, so it will likely be kept.
The ancient grain bread was publicly announced as the newest 'Meisterstück', creating a visible commitment that management would want to justify by keeping it.
